home-remodeling.meta_description: Mid-century Island City ranches in Wilton Manors rebuilt to current code, fully permitted and supervised daily. Call (786) 273-2524.
home-remodeling.hero_sub: Whole-home remodeling for Wilton Manors ranches and riverfront rebuilds: layouts opened, mechanicals replaced, impact glass installed. Permitted through Community Development Services, watched daily by the contractor whose license is on the job, Lic. CGC1539072.
intro_paragraphs: Wilton Manors had fewer than a thousand residents in 1950 and more than eight thousand by 1960, which tells you most of what you need to know about its housing stock. The Island City is largely concrete-block ranches and low-slung mid-century houses from that decade, plus the newer townhouses that reshaped Highland Estates and the water-facing homes along Jenada Isles and Middle River Manor. Owners here rarely tear down. They gut. Whole-house remodeling means taking out the wall between the galley kitchen and the Florida room, swapping jalousies for impact glass, and giving a compact plan some air.

Permits run through the City of Wilton Manors Community Development Services Department at 2020 Wilton Drive, filed on the Broward County Uniform Building Permit Application under the current Florida Building Code. The county is High-Velocity Hurricane Zone territory, which puts windows, doors, roofing and shutters on approved product listings backed by sealed wind-load calculations. The building officials and inspectors reviewing your job hold certifications from the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals, which also keeps Broward's amendments to the code's administrative chapter and rules on challenges to a building official's call. Full renovation submittals want a sealed survey less than two years old.

What we sell, mostly, is the absence of surprises. The scope is fixed in writing before demolition, with allowances that mean something. A supervisor is on site every working day. The finished half of the house gets papered, taped and defended from the half that is open. Twenty-plus years of South Florida construction sit behind that, along with 150-plus delivered remodels and additions, all of them permitted, all of them inspected, licensed and insured, Lic. CGC1539072. Lots sit close together here, so we keep to the city's posted construction hours and leave the street cleaner than we found it.
home-remodeling.scope_intro: Nothing gets opened before the line items are agreed. Below, the work that recurs on almost every Wilton Manors whole-house project.

scope_items.name: Ranch layouts, opened up
scope_items.desc: Removing the block partitions that separate kitchen, dining and Florida room, with beams engineered, calculations sealed, and the structural permit pulled before anything swings.

scope_items.name: Jalousies to impact glass
scope_items.desc: Louvered and single-pane openings replaced with approved impact windows and doors, sized to the existing block openings so the elevation still looks deliberate.

scope_items.name: Slab-era plumbing, replaced
scope_items.desc: Cast iron and galvanized lines under a 1950s slab traced, camera-inspected and replaced while the floors are open rather than discovered two years later.

scope_items.name: Panels, ducts and insulation
scope_items.desc: Service upgrades from mid-century amperage, ductwork resized for the actual load, and roof-deck insulation that a Broward August will quietly repay you for.

scope_items.name: Terrazzo, tile and millwork
scope_items.desc: Original terrazzo polished back where it survives, new stone and millwork where it does not, and trim scaled for eight-foot ceilings instead of ten.

faqs.q: Which department pulls the permit for a Wilton Manors remodel?
faqs.a: The City of Wilton Manors Community Development Services Department, Construction Services division, at 2020 Wilton Drive. Applications go in online on the Broward County Uniform Building Permit Application, and the review stops are building, zoning, public utilities and whichever trades your scope touches. Inspection requests are submitted online before 4:30 p.m. for the next business day. A full renovation submittal also wants a survey sealed within the last two years and a signed impervious calculation.

faqs.q: Is there a design review board that has to approve my plans?
faqs.a: For an ordinary single-family remodel, no. Wilton Manors has a Planning and Zoning Board, a Development Review Committee and a Historic Preservation Board created by ordinance, but a house that stays inside its existing footprint and setbacks is a plan review matter, not a hearing. You land in front of a board when you need a variance, a site plan, a rezoning or a plat change. We tell you which category you are in during the first walk-through, before drawings cost money.

faqs.q: What does the Board of Rules and Appeals actually do to my project?
faqs.a: Mostly it works upstream of you. Broward's Board of Rules and Appeals certifies the building officials, inspectors and plans examiners assigned to your job. It keeps the county's amendments to the administrative chapter of the Florida Building Code, settles arguments over what a contested code section actually means, and takes the appeal when an official rules against you. You will never attend a meeting over a kitchen. You feel it in how consistently Broward inspectors read the same code.

faqs.q: How long does a whole-house remodel in Wilton Manors take?
faqs.a: Drawings and engineering tend to take a couple of months. Permitting adds weeks on top, depending on how clean the submittal is. Construction on a full gut of a mid-century house commonly runs six months to a year. Long-lead cabinetry and impact glass shape the calendar more than framing does, which is why we order early. A written schedule ships with the estimate, and the daily supervisor is the reason it survives.

faqs.q: What should a full renovation cost on a house like mine?
faqs.a: It depends on how much of the house you keep. Refinishing and re-skinning a sound ranch is one budget. New roof, new impact openings, new electrical service, new under-slab plumbing and a reorganized floor plan is a different exercise entirely. We price from a specification after walking the house, never from a per-square-foot rule of thumb. PGX competes on a number that holds through the job, not on being the cheapest of three quotes.

home-remodeling.cta_sub: Start with a walk-through. We look, we ask the awkward questions, and a fixed-scope written estimate follows, in English o en español.

kitchen-remodeling.title: Wilton Manors, FL Kitchen Renovation | PGX Builders
kitchen-remodeling.meta_description: Wilton Manors kitchen remodeling for closed mid-century ranches. Beams in, pass-through out, cabinetry made not bought. (786) 273-2524.
kitchen-remodeling.hero_sub: Custom cabinetry, stone counters and the structural opening that connects a closed 1950s kitchen to the rest of the house. Permitted through the city, inspected at every trade, supervised daily.
kitchen-remodeling.local_heading: Where the wall used to be
intro_paragraphs: Mid-century builders in Wilton Manors put the kitchen in a corner and shut the door on it. Walk a ranch off NE 26th Street, or a block in Coral Estates, and you find the same plan repeated: a galley barely wide enough for two people, a pass-through to the dining room, and a Florida room next door doing very little. The kitchen remodeling projects we take on here almost always begin by removing that wall, then rebuilding the room around an island four people can sit at.

A kitchen at this level pulls building, electrical, plumbing and mechanical into one submittal, so it clears all four review stops at Wilton Manors Community Development Services and gets inspected at each rough-in. Two things surprise owners of 1950s slab houses. First, the electrical service: a panel sized for a 1958 range and a window unit will not carry induction, a double oven and a wine column. Second, what sits under the slab, because original cast iron has to be cut out, replaced and inspected before anyone pours back. Enlarge the window over the sink and High-Velocity Hurricane Zone product approvals join the set.

Cabinet shops do their sharpest work for builders who field-measure after framing and before ordering, and who template stone from the installed boxes rather than from a drawing. That is how we sequence a kitchen. Cabinetry and appliances with long lead times get ordered up front, so nobody is living around an open room while a truck crosses Georgia. Floors, doors and the route from the driveway get protected every morning, not once at the start. One fixed written scope, one supervisor, one company answering the phone from estimate through warranty.
kitchen-remodeling.scope_heading: Scope of a Wilton Manors kitchen
kitchen-remodeling.scope_intro: Priced line by line before a single cabinet is ordered. Five items usually account for the bulk of an Island City kitchen budget.

scope_items.name: Cabinetry made, not bought
scope_items.desc: Made-to-order boxes and doors detailed for eight-foot mid-century ceilings, finished for Broward humidity, with fillers and scribes cut on site rather than caulked over.

scope_items.name: Islands engineered, not stacked
scope_items.desc: Quartzite, marble or porcelain templated after the cabinets are set, with seating overhangs carried on steel or brackets instead of optimism.

scope_items.name: Taking down the pass-through
scope_items.desc: Opening the block wall between kitchen and dining or Florida room, sized by an engineer, with a permitted beam and a bearing detail that reaches the footing.

scope_items.name: Service and circuits upgraded
scope_items.desc: A new panel and, where the load calls for it, a heavier service, plus dedicated circuits for induction, double ovens, refrigeration and the outlets nobody planned for.

scope_items.name: Venting that actually vents
scope_items.desc: A hood ducted through the roof or wall to code, sealed and balanced, instead of a recirculating filter politely returning grease to the room.

faqs.q: Does a kitchen remodel here really need a permit?
faqs.a: Anything past paint and a like-for-like appliance swap does. Moving plumbing, adding circuits, changing a hood duct or taking out a wall all get permitted through Community Development Services, with separate trade reviews and inspections. The upside is a record. When you sell, the buyer's inspector finds a permitted kitchen instead of a mystery, and permitting something retroactively always costs more than sequencing it correctly the first time.

faqs.q: Can the kitchen open into the Florida room?
faqs.a: Usually, and in Wilton Manors it is the single most requested change. These are concrete-block houses, so the opening needs an engineer to size a beam and detail how the load travels down to the footing. That drawing goes in with the permit set and is inspected before it is covered. Occasionally a wall carries something awkward, like a plumbing stack or a duct main, and the honest answer is a wide cased opening rather than a full removal.

faqs.q: How long is my kitchen out of service?
faqs.a: Plan on roughly two months of construction for a full kitchen, longer when structure or a service upgrade is in the scope. The clock that matters starts earlier: custom cabinetry and stone are ordered months ahead, and we will not demolish anything until the cabinets have a confirmed delivery date. Most clients rig a hot plate and a fridge out in the carport or Florida room and stay put for the duration.

faqs.q: Does my kitchen have to meet hurricane code?
faqs.a: The cabinetry does not. The openings do. Every exterior opening in Broward is a High-Velocity Hurricane Zone opening, so if the scope enlarges a window, adds a door to the patio or changes a slider, the unit needs an approved product listing and the installation needs sealed engineering. Copies of the product approvals go into the permit package with the plans. We handle that paperwork so the kitchen is not a conversation at your next insurance inspection.

faqs.q: What does a high-end kitchen run here?
faqs.a: Selections drive it far more than square footage. Custom cabinetry, natural stone and a serious appliance package can absorb most of a budget before a single trade shows up, and structural work or a service upgrade sits on top of that. We scope in writing after a walk-through, which means you are pricing a specification instead of a hopeful round number. We are not the low bid, and we would rather say so in the first meeting.

kitchen-remodeling.cta_sub: Tell us how you cook and what the current room refuses to do. The written scope that comes back is fixed, in English o en español.

bathroom-remodeling.title: Bathroom Remodeling in Wilton Manors, FL | PGX Builders
bathroom-remodeling.meta_description: Wilton Manors bath remodels: a second bathroom carved out of the plan, membranes flood-tested, heavy glass on real blocking. Call (786) 273-2524.
bathroom-remodeling.hero_sub: Primary suites, frameless showers and freestanding tubs for Wilton Manors homes built when one bath per house was standard. Waterproofed to spec, permitted, inspected, and supervised by the licensed contractor who signed the estimate.
intro_paragraphs: The typical Wilton Manors house arrived with one full bath and, if the original owners were feeling generous, a half off the hall. That worked in 1957. It does not work for anyone who has since seen a modern primary suite. So the common project across Westside, the Central Area and the Three Bridges streets is subtraction and addition at once: a third bedroom or an oversized closet gives up floor area, the hall bath grows into it, and what emerges is a suite with a double vanity, a shower you can turn around in, and a tub that stands on its own.

Bathroom remodeling in Wilton Manors is permitted through Community Development Services, and the job gets inspected by discipline as it goes: plumbing, electrical, mechanical. That sequence is the whole point, because waterproofing is verified before tile hides it. The local complication is the slab. These houses sit on grade with cast iron drains cast into concrete, so a relocated toilet or a recessed curbless pan means saw-cutting, re-routing and re-pouring. Add a window for daylight and Broward's High-Velocity Hurricane Zone product rules apply to the unit and to how it is fastened.

No room in the house is smaller or less forgiving. Pans are flood-tested and left overnight before anyone opens a box of tile. Slopes get checked with a level rather than a hopeful glance. Blocking goes into the walls for heavy glass and for grab bars you may not want yet. Every job carries a fixed written scope, a supervisor who shows up daily, and a license and insurance that are current, Lic. CGC1539072, with permits and inspections on all of it. Beautiful tile over bad waterproofing is a countdown, not a renovation.
bathroom-remodeling.scope_heading: The bath scope on a slab house
bathroom-remodeling.scope_intro: Scoped in writing before the tile order goes in, because changing your mind at rough-in is the expensive kind of change. The usual components below.

scope_items.name: Bedroom traded for a suite
scope_items.desc: Reworking bedroom, closet and hall bath into one suite, with new rough-ins, framing and a permit set drawn to match the plan you actually approved.

scope_items.name: Curbless pans in a slab
scope_items.desc: Recessing the pan into a 1950s slab where the drain line and structure allow, with a linear drain, and a low-profile alternative offered honestly when they do not.

scope_items.name: Membranes filled and tested
scope_items.desc: Bonded sheet or liquid membranes with corners and penetrations detailed, then filled and left overnight so any leak announces itself before the marble arrives.

scope_items.name: Heavy glass on real blocking
scope_items.desc: Frameless enclosures hung from blocking installed during framing, with hinge locations set before drywall closes rather than negotiated with a glazier afterward.

scope_items.name: Exhaust routed outside
scope_items.desc: Quiet fans ducted through a low-slope mid-century roof to a proper cap, so humidity leaves the building instead of touring the attic space.

faqs.q: Which parts of a bathroom job get inspected?
faqs.a: More than owners expect, and that is a feature. On a permitted bath remodel through Community Development Services you will see a plumbing rough, an electrical rough, framing where walls moved, mechanical for the exhaust, then finals by discipline. Waterproofing is looked at before tile covers it, which is the inspection that saves you. Requests filed online before 4:30 p.m. land the next business day, so a small bathroom does not stall waiting for a visit.

faqs.q: Is a curbless shower realistic on a slab house?
faqs.a: Often, but the slab decides, not the photograph. Recessing a pan means saw-cutting concrete, relocating the drain and re-pouring, and on some 1950s houses the existing line depth makes that a poor trade. When it works, it is worth doing properly. When it does not, a low curb with a correctly pitched pan and a linear drain reads almost identically and costs far less to build right.

faqs.q: The house still has cast iron drains. Do we replace them?
faqs.a: If the floor is already open, replace them. Cast iron installed during the Wilton Manors building boom is at or past its service life, and the failure mode is a slow leak under a slab you have just retiled. We run a camera down the lines early, so the call gets made on evidence instead of instinct. Handling it while the floor is open costs a fraction of handling it after the stone is set and the glass is hung.

faqs.q: Can we add a window without triggering a hurricane-code problem?
faqs.a: You can add one, but it turns into a code item. Any new or enlarged exterior opening in Broward is a High-Velocity Hurricane Zone opening, which means an approved impact unit, a sealed installation detail and a wind-load calculation in the permit set. Obscure impact glass buys privacy and daylight with nothing to close before a storm. It adds a step to the drawings, not a month to the schedule.

faqs.q: How much does a primary bath at this level cost?
faqs.a: Wide range, and honestly so. Fixtures, stone and heavy glass set the visible cost. The plumbing rerouting, waterproofing and framing behind them set the real one, and slab work moves the number more than clients expect. We walk the space, scope what the building genuinely needs rather than what a catalog suggests, and put a fixed price on it. Finish work at this level is what we do; low bidding is not.

bathroom-remodeling.cta_sub: Show us the room, the plumbing wall and the wish list. Back comes the scope, the sequence and the price, in English o en español.

home-additions.title: Home Additions in Wilton Manors, FL | PGX Builders Group
home-additions.meta_description: Island City lots are tight, not finished. Rear extensions, second stories and carport conversions in Wilton Manors, FL. (786) 273-2524.
home-additions.h1: More room on a small lot
home-additions.hero_sub: Rear extensions, second stories, carport conversions and in-law suites in Wilton Manors: engineered, zoned, permitted through Community Development Services and built by a licensed, insured general contractor who is on site daily.
home-additions.local_heading: Where the addition can actually go
intro_paragraphs: Wilton Manors covers 1.97 square miles, platted for single-story houses on modest lots, which makes a home addition a puzzle before it is a project. The moves that work are well known by now: pushing a family room and primary suite into the rear yard, converting the carport everyone parks in front of anyway, adding a second story over a ranch in Highland Estates or Coral Estates, or building a self-contained in-law suite. On the water in Jenada Isles and along Middle River Manor, the addition wants to face the river and the glass follows it.

Zoning is the first gate, not the last. Wilton Manors caps impervious coverage in its single-family districts, at 50 percent of the lot in RS-5, so new roof area, a wider driveway and a pool deck all compete for the same allowance, and a signed impervious calculation is part of the submittal. Community Development Services also wants a sealed survey under two years old, soil tests, an elevation certificate with base flood elevation, sealed wind-load calculations, and, where it applies, approval from the Broward County Environmental Protection and Growth Management Department. Anything needing a variance or site plan goes to the Development Review Committee and the Planning and Zoning Board.

You can read a builder's habits straight off an addition. New footings have to marry old ones, the tie-beam has to run continuous, and the seam where fresh stucco meets 1950s stucco should be impossible to find in raking afternoon light. We stage the work so the family keeps a working kitchen and bathroom, hold the site to the city's construction hours, and hand back a house that reads as one building rather than two. Fixed written scope. Daily supervision. One accountable team carrying the job from feasibility study to final inspection to warranty.
home-additions.scope_intro: Every addition starts with a current survey, an engineer and an honest look at the coverage limits. These are the five we build most often.

scope_items.name: Pushing into the back yard
scope_items.desc: The rear of a small house extended on new footings, with tie-beam continuation and the roof joint drawn into one coordinated permit set.

scope_items.name: Carports turned into rooms
scope_items.desc: Converting the open carport most 1950s plans included into conditioned space, with insulation, impact openings, mechanical extension and square footage that legally counts.

scope_items.name: Building a second story
scope_items.desc: Testing existing footings and block walls first, then designing an upper level the engineer, the zoning reviewer and the roofline can all live with.

scope_items.name: Self-contained family suites
scope_items.desc: Independent bedroom, bath and kitchenette wings for parents or long-staying relatives, built to code and detailed so the addition never announces itself from the street.

scope_items.name: Coverage and drainage math
scope_items.desc: Impervious calculations, swales and site drainage resolved before design locks, since a driveway and a pool deck spend the same allowance the addition needs.

faqs.q: How much of my lot can I actually build on in Wilton Manors?
faqs.a: Less than most owners assume, and the binding number is usually impervious coverage rather than the building footprint alone. In the RS-5 single-family district the city allows 50 percent of the property to be impervious, and the permit package includes a signed impervious and pervious calculation. Roof area, driveway, walkways, patio, pool and slabs all count toward it. We run that math at feasibility so nobody designs a wing the site cannot carry.

faqs.q: Do I have to raise my seawall if I add on to a waterfront house?
faqs.a: Very possibly. The city's 2020 seawall ordinance requires waterfront owners to bring seawalls up to the city's standard when new construction or substantial renovation takes place, and separately when tidal flooding or erosion starts spilling onto a neighbor or the roadway. Seawall work also carries its own permit path through Broward County environmental licensing on top of the city permit. Budget it as part of the addition rather than discovering it at plan review.

faqs.q: Can my 1950s block house take a second story?
faqs.a: Sometimes yes, sometimes with reinforcement, occasionally not without spending more than the space is worth. A structural engineer evaluates the existing footings, block and tie-beam, and whether the roof framing can come off cleanly. We get that answer early, with numbers attached, and we will tell you plainly when a rear extension buys the same square footage for materially less. Guessing at this stage is how projects go sideways.

faqs.q: Will an addition go before a city board?
faqs.a: Only if it needs something discretionary. A conforming addition that respects setbacks, height and coverage is reviewed by building and zoning staff without a hearing. Ask for a variance, a site plan approval, a rezoning or a plat change and it goes to the Development Review Committee, which meets monthly, and then the Planning and Zoning Board. Board months add real calendar time, so we design toward conformity wherever the program allows it.

faqs.q: How long from first sketch to finished addition?
faqs.a: Design and engineering typically run two to three months. Permitting adds more, depending on submittal quality and any board hearings. Construction on a substantial addition commonly runs six months or beyond, and waterfront lots carrying county environmental review take longer still. We put the whole sequence in the written schedule that comes with the estimate, including the stretches that sit in someone else's hands.

outdoor-living.meta_description: Terraces, summer kitchens, docks and seawalls in Wilton Manors, FL. Middle River waterfront work licensed by city and Broward County. (786) 273-2524.
outdoor-living.h1: The river side of the house
outdoor-living.hero_sub: Terraces, summer kitchens, pergolas, driveways, docks and seawalls along the Middle River, designed within Wilton Manors coverage limits, licensed through city and Broward County, and built by an insured general contractor.
outdoor-living.local_heading: Living on the North and South Forks
intro_paragraphs: Wilton Manors is wrapped by the North and South Forks of the Middle River, which is where the Island City nickname comes from and why so much of the good exterior work here faces water. A Jenada Isles back yard wants a dock, a lift and a shaded terrace between the seawall and the house. Inland, off NE 26th Street or through the Central Area, outdoor living means a summer kitchen against the old carport wall, shade over the pool deck, and a driveway that finally stops looking like 1958.

A Wilton Manors backyard runs into two limits quickly. The first is coverage: the RS-5 district allows 50 percent of the lot to be impervious, and patios, walkways, pool decks and driveways all draw on that same account, with a signed calculation in the permit file. The second is the water. Docks, seawalls and boat lifts need a sealed survey, sealed engineering and a license from Broward County's Aquatic and Wetland Resources Program, plus confirmation that the state, the Army Corps and the South Florida Water Management District have either reviewed the work or delegated it. Lights and lifts add an electrical permit; driven pilings add a special inspector.

Exterior construction gets built to interior standards on our jobs. Gas, water and power for a summer kitchen are permitted trades, not weekend work. Pergola footings are engineered for Broward wind loads and the connections are detailed on paper before anyone digs a hole. Terraces are pitched to move rainy-season water away from the slab, and hardware near brackish water is specified for brackish water. We work inside the city's construction hours, keep the mess off the street and out of the neighbor's hedge, and warranty what we build.
outdoor-living.scope_intro: One coordinated permit set instead of four trades blaming each other. These are the exterior elements Wilton Manors owners ask for most.

scope_items.name: Summer kitchens, permitted properly
scope_items.desc: Outdoor kitchens with inspected gas, water and electrical, weather-rated cabinetry, and stone chosen to survive humidity, sun and a decade of salt-tinged air.

scope_items.name: Dockage and seawall work
scope_items.desc: Waterfront structures engineered and licensed through the city and Broward County, including the separate electrical permit that dock lights and boat lifts require.

scope_items.name: Shade structures, engineered
scope_items.desc: Pergolas, trellises and covered terraces with footings sized for uplift and every connection detailed to the wind loads this county actually enforces.

scope_items.name: Paving against the allowance
scope_items.desc: Pavers, finished concrete and pool surrounds laid out against the impervious allowance, with swales and drainage handled so water leaves the lot the right way.

scope_items.name: Stucco, paint and re-roof timing
scope_items.desc: Envelope work sequenced with the roof so scaffolding, roofing product approvals and the window and door submittals all get handled in a single pass.

faqs.q: What does it take to permit a dock or seawall in Wilton Manors?
faqs.a: More agencies than owners expect. The city needs a structural permit with a survey under two years old and sealed engineering. Broward County's Aquatic and Wetland Resources Program licenses work in, on or under surface waters. The state, the Army Corps and the South Florida Water Management District each have a role, though the county frequently holds delegated authority for their review. Dock lights and lifts add an electrical permit, and driven pilings add a special inspector form.

faqs.q: Is my seawall my responsibility?
faqs.a: Almost certainly. Seawalls in Wilton Manors are overwhelmingly privately owned, and the city depends on owners to raise them. Its 2020 ordinance calls for a seawall to be brought to a five-foot standard when new construction or substantial renovation happens on the property, and also when unimpeded tidal flooding or erosion begins affecting a neighbor or the roadway. If major work is already planned, deal with the wall inside the same project.

faqs.q: Can I pave the whole back yard for a pool deck and patio?
faqs.a: No, and the ceiling arrives sooner than people think. The RS-5 single-family district allows 50 percent of the property to be impervious, and the house, driveway, walkways, patio, pool and any slabs all count toward that. Permeable pavers, planted borders and gravel zones can buy room back when they are detailed correctly. We run the calculation during design, because redrawing a terrace after plan review is nobody's favorite week.

faqs.q: How big a boat can I keep behind the house?
faqs.a: The Middle River answers that, not the dock. Bridges cross both forks inside the city, so air draft governs what can reach your seawall from the Intracoastal as much as water depth does. Owners along these canals tend to run center consoles, day boats and smaller cruisers rather than sportfishermen. We will build the dock and lift for the boat that can actually get home, and we will say so before you buy either one.

faqs.q: What should a full backyard project cost?
faqs.a: It scales with utilities, structure and water. New paving and landscape lighting sit at one end of the range. A roofed outdoor room, a summer kitchen with live gas and water, a pool, a dock and a rebuilt seawall sit at the other, and waterfront permitting adds calendar as well as cost. We walk the site, write the specification, then attach one number to it. Square-foot rules of thumb do not survive contact with a canal.

permitting-compliance.local_heading: Where the record lives, and who reads it
intro_paragraphs: Wilton Manors filled in fast after 1950, and the paperwork did not always keep pace. The Island City's concrete-block ranches have absorbed seventy years of work from owners, handymen and contractors of wildly different habits. So the carport that quietly became a bedroom in Coral Estates, the Florida room glassed in over on Middle River Manor, the service panel upgraded off the books, the dock or lift added behind a Jenada Isles house all land in one category. The house looks finished. The city's file says the job never ended, and a title search will find it.

Permits are issued by the Construction Services division of Community Development Services at 2020 Wilton Drive, filed through the city's online permitting portal on the Broward County Uniform Building Permit Application, with a Notice of Commencement where the work calls for one. Broward then adds a layer above the city: the county Board of Rules and Appeals writes the local amendments your plans examiner applies, certifies the inspector who walks the job, and issues the formal reading when a code section is argued over. Every inch of the county is High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so glazing, doors and roofing travel with approved products and their anchor details.

PGX Builders Group has twenty-plus years in South Florida behind it and more than 150 permitted, inspected remodels and additions delivered, which in practice means we have read a great many of other people's files. We pull the history on the address before quoting anything, open up what has to be seen, and bring in the engineer, architect or surveyor the record demands instead of pretending to be one. On the river side we look at floodplain exposure early, because a deep renovation can cross into substantial improvement. The supervisor who ran the work meets the inspector. We do not sell shortcuts, and there are none to sell.
permitting-compliance.scope_heading: What we file and what we fix
permitting-compliance.scope_intro: Half of this work starts as a plan. The other half starts as something a previous owner left behind. Both begin the same way: read the record, then price it.

scope_items.name: Permits left open
scope_items.desc: Reading the full permit history the city holds for the address, matching it against what is actually standing, then reviving, amending or re-inspecting until the city marks the file closed.

scope_items.name: Work nobody ever filed
scope_items.desc: The enclosed carport, the glassed-in porch, the bathroom that simply appeared: surveyed and documented as built, engineered where the structure demands it, inspected against the code in force today.

scope_items.name: Impact products, approved
scope_items.desc: Windows, doors and roof assemblies matched to approvals valid in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, with the anchor schedule the approval specifies rather than whatever the last crew used.

scope_items.name: Inspections to a signed final
scope_items.desc: Each phase requested in an order the house can deliver, a PGX supervisor on site to meet the inspector, and the final signed so the permit stops being your problem.

scope_items.name: Docks, seawalls and lifts
scope_items.desc: Middle River structures built or legalized with a sealed survey, sealed engineering, county environmental licensing, and the separate electrical permit that lighting and lifts require.

faqs.q: There is an open permit on my Wilton Manors house and we close soon. What now?
faqs.a: Start with the record. The address history shows every permit ever pulled, which inspections were signed, and exactly where things stopped. Then it is a diagnosis. Sometimes only the final was never called. Sometimes what stands does not match what was approved. Sometimes the permit sits under a contractor who is long gone. All three are solvable, none of them over a weekend, so the call belongs weeks ahead of funding rather than days.

faqs.q: Who issues the permit here, and how do inspections get scheduled?
faqs.a: Construction Services, the permitting arm of Community Development Services, works out of City Hall at 2020 Wilton Drive. Everything is filed digitally through the city's online permitting portal on Broward's uniform application, then routed to building, zoning, utilities and whichever trade reviewers the scope pulls in. Inspections are requested online against the city's daily cutoff, so we file each one when the phase is genuinely ready rather than to chase an open slot. When the last one is signed, a certificate of completion or occupancy closes the file.

faqs.q: What actually needs a permit on a house like mine?
faqs.a: More than most owners expect. Structural changes, roofing, windows and doors, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, pools, fences, decks, driveways and demolition all do. Interior paint, flooring laid over a sound slab and swapping a fixture for its equal generally do not. What tends to go unfiled is exactly what gets expensive later: an enclosed carport, a jalousie-to-impact swap, a relocated water heater, a heavier electrical service, a lift on the river.

faqs.q: Does recertification or a milestone inspection apply to my property?
faqs.a: Not to a single-family house. Broward's building safety inspection program is administered through the county Board of Rules and Appeals, keys off building age, and leaves one- and two-family dwellings out. Florida's milestone inspection and structural integrity reserve study rules reach condominium and cooperative buildings of three habitable stories or more, which here means a handful of older low-rise buildings, not the ranches. The report belongs to a licensed engineer or architect. We engage one, then permit and build the repairs it calls for.

faqs.q: What does it cost to put unpermitted work right?
faqs.a: It depends on what is behind the drywall. If the construction is sound and only the final was never called, this is a modest line item and some patience. A room framed over a patio slab with no engineering behind it, or an opening cut through a bearing wall, can mean taking it apart and rebuilding to current code. Permit fees are the city's and scale with the value of the work. You get the number and the bad news in the same written scope.
